editorial:
Imagine trying to find yourself while the person who knows you best is slowly forgetting who you are. That is exactly what you get in this moving story. You follow a young man who is keeping his sexuality a secret from the world, feeling stuck in his own skin. At the same time, he has to step up and take care of his mother, who is fighting early onset Alzheimer's. It is a heavy setup, but the vibe is more about love and growth than just sadness. You will feel for these characters as they navigate a house filled with memories that are fading away.

The acting is what really makes this work, as the lead actors make you feel every bit of their frustration and hope. The pacing is slow and steady, giving you time to breathe, though some parts might feel a bit long. If you enjoy stories that tug at your heartstrings, you need to see this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small emotional details. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the son finally comes out to his mother during one of her rare moments of total clarity. She tells him she always knew and loves him regardless. This gives him the confidence to stop hiding and start living his own life. The movie ends with him moving into his own place while still caring for her, showing that he found peace with his identity and his mother's illness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful family stories and character growth.
